claims.claim: Complement equivalence and exact endpoint cases. Let F(n,k) count labelled graphs on [n] with vertex-cover number at most k, let N=binom(n,2), and put m=n−k. For 0≤k≤n, F(n,k)=2^N−T(n,m), where T(n,m) is the number of labelled K_m-free graphs. Consequently F(n,n−3)=2^N−T(n,3), with T(n,3) the triangle-free graph count. Also F(n,0)=1; F(n,1)=1+n(2^{n−1}−1)−binom(n,2); F(n,n−2)=2^N−1; and F(n,n−1)=F(n,n)=2^N.
claims.evidence: For every graph G, C is a vertex cover iff V(G)\C is independent, hence τ(G)=n−α(G). Thus τ(G)≤k iff G has an independent m-set, and complementation bijects the failing graphs with K_m-free graphs. The endpoint formulas follow for m=n,2,1,0. For k=1, each nonempty admissible graph is a subgraph of a labelled star; one-edge graphs are counted twice among the n star sums and every graph with at least two edges has a unique center, giving the stated correction.
claims.witness: Exhaustive enumeration of every labelled graph for 1≤n≤6 verified the complement identity for every 0≤k≤n and every stated endpoint formula.
claims.search_method: Direct proof from the cover/independent-set equivalence, followed by exhaustive exact enumeration.

claims.claim: There is a deterministic exact algorithm using polynomial space and time 2^{q+O(n)}, where q=binom(n,2)−binom(n−k,2)=kn−k(k+1)/2. Therefore the target is achieved whenever k=o(n), including k=O(n/log n).
claims.evidence: For a fixed k-set C, exactly q=binom(k,2)+k(n−k) edge positions are allowed when C is a cover. Enumerating all such graphs for every C and retaining a graph only for its first k-cover counts every graph with τ≤k exactly once, since every smaller cover can be extended to size k. Testing all k-sets for canonicality gives at most poly(n)·binom(n,k)^2·2^q=2^{q+O(n)} time. Iterators, one graph mask, and the at-most-N-bit answer require polynomial space. Since q≤nk, q+O(n)=o(n²) when k=o(n).
claims.witness: For all n≤6 and all k, exhaustive simulation confirmed that the first-k-cover rule accepts exactly F(n,k) graphs and that both formulas for q agree.
claims.search_method: Symbolic enumeration and complexity analysis, with exhaustive canonical-generation checks.

claims.claim: For every fixed k there is a polynomial-time exact algorithm. More explicitly, F(n,k) is computable in time at most poly(n)·sum_{t=0}^k binom(n,t)·2^{binom(t,2)+t}·[2(t+2)]^{2^t−1}.
claims.evidence: Fix a candidate t-cover C, put I=[n]\C, and fix H=G[C]. Any cover D determines X=C\D and Y=D∩I. It is valid only if X is H-independent and U_X⊆Y, while (C\X)∪U_X is always a cover for such X. Hence C is minimum exactly when |U_X|≥|X| for every nonempty H-independent X. Equality gives every alternative minimum cover, and comparison of the increasing vertex sequences shows C is earlier exactly when min X<min U_X. The DP's capped cardinality and earlier-label bit therefore contain precisely the information needed. There are at most 2^t−1 coordinates, at most 2(t+2) states per coordinate, and 2^t neighborhood transitions per outside vertex. Summation over C, H, and t gives the displayed fixed-parameter factor and polynomial dependence on n.
claims.witness: The characterization was checked for every candidate cover of every labelled graph with n≤6. An independent implementation of the capped-state DP matched F(n,k) for every n≤6 and k≤3.
claims.search_method: Derived every alternative cover from its exchanged sets X and Y, proved the lexicographic criterion, and independently implemented the resulting exact DP.

claims.claim: Exact first- and second-moment formulas give certified bounds for all parameters. For 1≤m≤n, let q=N−binom(m,2), S1=binom(n,m)2^q, and S2=binom(n,m)·sum_{j=max(0,2m−n)}^m binom(m,j)binom(n−m,m−j)2^{N−2binom(m,2)+binom(j,2)}. Then max{2^q, ceil(S1²/S2)}≤F(n,n−m)≤min{2^N,S1}. In particular, q≤log₂F(n,n−m)≤q+n.
claims.evidence: If X(G) counts independent m-sets, summing over a selected set gives Σ_G X(G)=binom(n,m)2^q=S1. For an ordered pair S,T with intersection size j, exactly 2binom(m,2)−binom(j,2) distinct edges are forbidden, which gives the stated S2=Σ_G X(G)^2. The indicator inequality 1_{X>0}≤X yields the upper bound; Cauchy–Schwarz yields S1²≤F·S2; and fixing one independent m-set yields F≥2^q. Finally binom(n,m)≤2^n proves the logarithmic upper bound.
claims.witness: Exact exhaustive sums of X(G) and X(G)^2 agreed with S1 and S2 for every 1≤m≤n≤6; all integer-rounded bounds also held.
claims.search_method: Direct ordered-pair counting and exact Cauchy–Schwarz derivation, followed by exhaustive moment calculations.

claims.claim: At the triangle-free endpoint, a substantial subclass is exactly countable in polynomial time. Let B_n be the number of labelled bipartite graphs and P_n=sum_{a=0}^n binom(n,a)2^{a(n−a)}. Then B_0=1 and B_n=(P_n−sum_{a=1}^{n−1}binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a})/2. Hence F(n,n−3)≤2^N−B_n is an exact-arithmetic, polynomial-time computable bound.
claims.evidence: P_n counts ordered proper two-colorings together with their graph, so a bipartite graph with c connected components has weight 2^c. The convolution independently gives the same weight: choose a labelled block A and bipartite graphs on A and its complement, which is equivalent to assigning every connected component wholly to one of two blocks. Thus P_n=Σ_a binom(n,a)B_aB_{n−a}; the two endpoint terms are both B_n, proving the recurrence. Its integers have O(n²) bits and it uses polynomially many arithmetic operations. Since every bipartite graph is triangle-free, T(n,3)≥B_n and the asserted upper bound follows.
claims.witness: The recurrence produced B_0,…,B_6 = 1,1,2,7,41,376,5177, exactly matching exhaustive bipartiteness tests; the resulting bound also held for n=3,…,6.
claims.search_method: Weighted double counting by connected components, bit-complexity analysis, and exhaustive exact verification.

claims.claim: There is a two-sided explicit-enumeration obstruction near the opposite endpoint, with its exact boundary at m=3. For 2≤m≤n, put r=m−1, write n=ar+b with 0≤b<r, and let t_r(n)=[n²−b(a+1)²−(r−b)a²]/2. Then 2^{N−binom(m,2)}≤F(n,n−m) and 2^{t_r(n)}≤2^N−F(n,n−m)=T(n,m). Hence, for every fixed m≥3, both the counted and excluded families have size 2^{Ω(n²)}. In particular, at k=n−3, F(n,n−3)≥2^{N−3} and T(n,3)≥2^{floor(n²/4)}. Thus neither member-by-member enumeration of the target family nor of its complement can give a 2^{o(n²)} algorithm; a successful uniform algorithm must aggregate graphs. This obstruction does not rule out such aggregation.
claims.evidence: Fixing one independent m-set leaves N−binom(m,2) arbitrary edges, proving the first lower bound. A balanced partition into r=m−1 parts has exactly t_r(n) cross-part pairs; every subgraph of the corresponding complete r-partite graph is K_m-free, giving 2^{t_r(n)} distinct excluded graphs. For fixed m≥3 both exponents are Θ(n²), while for m=2 the construction has t_1(n)=0 and T(n,2)=1. At m=3 the balanced two-part exponent is floor(n²/4). Explicitly visiting every member of either family therefore takes quadratic-exponent time in the standard sequential model, without excluding compressed aggregation.
claims.witness: For every 2≤m≤n≤6, exact enumeration verified both lower bounds and the balanced-partition formula; the m=3 specializations and m=2 boundary were also checked.
claims.search_method: Explicit independent-set and balanced multipartite constructions, asymptotic exponent calculation, and exhaustive exact checks.

target_evidence: The source asks for an exact 2^{o(n²)} algorithm uniformly over the input k. The draft rigorously supplies such running times only when k=o(n), plus fixed-k algorithms, identities, bounds, and an obstruction to explicit enumeration. It explicitly leaves linear-k regimes—most notably k=n−3—without a subquadratic-exponent exact algorithm. Thus it makes material correct progress but does not resolve the entire target, and its stated PARTIAL resolution is accurate.
